content.tldr: Quantization compresses model weights from 16-bit floats to 4-bit or 8-bit integers, where GGUF targets CPU/mixed execution while GPTQ and AWQ optimize GPU serving.
content.simple_explanation: Standard LLM weights are stored as 16-bit floating point numbers (FP16 or BF16), requiring 2 bytes of VRAM per parameter (e.g. 14GB for a 7B model). Post-Training Quantization (PTQ) maps continuous floats to low-bit integers (INT8, INT4). GGUF is a binary file format optimized by llama.cpp for CPU offloading and consumer hardware. GPTQ performs second-order Taylor expansion calibration layer-by-layer for GPU inference. AWQ (Activation-aware Weight Quantization) observes that protecting the top 1% most salient weight channels avoids perplexity degradation without full calibration.
content.real_world_example: Converting a 24-bit high-resolution audio recording to a compressed MP3 format: human ears cannot discern subtle harmonic losses, but file size shrinks by 75%, allowing playback on mobile devices.
content.why_it_matters_and_pitfalls: Quantization allows a 70B parameter model to run on a single 48GB GPU instead of requiring an expensive multi-GPU cluster. Naive uniform rounding causes severe perplexity collapse, making activation-aware methods like AWQ essential for INT4.
